**Accept RI205’s four-maxima theorem at the observed handoff pins. No mathematical blocker found.**

The substantive checks pass:

- The retained-cap denominator lemma applies specifically to \(S=A+i\), with \(E_i\subseteq A\). It correctly repairs the missing coverage of the retained cap; it does **not** claim an all-ideal lemma on \(Q_i\). Full four-parent denominators in double sectors use the separate all-ideal floor. [Main proof, lines 145–219](</Volumes/AI_DATA/development/det-review-evidence/ri205-native-four-maxima-7gkvoked/FOUR_MAXIMA.md:145>)
- The support argument is valid: four Ferrers maxima require at least ten cells. A largest induced Ferrers suborder therefore misses an original maximum; restoring it raises defect. The marked diamond connects that role to every other proper role of the same terminal. This forces only the **canonical boundary** coefficient to zero and preserves positive \(\theta\). No false heredity assumption is used. [Companion, lines 27–83](</Volumes/AI_DATA/development/det-review-evidence/ri205-native-four-maxima-7gkvoked/FOUR_OMISSION_LEMMA.md:27>)
- Extra old maxima are correctly retained. The \(|X|=1,2\) parity factors have the stated parent sizes and bounds. Original coverage limits total old-vertex occurrences across the four triples to two, giving \(\Gamma\le243\,110^7\). [Lines 128–206](</Volumes/AI_DATA/development/det-review-evidence/ri205-native-four-maxima-7gkvoked/FOUR_OMISSION_LEMMA.md:128>)
- The cancellation multiplicities are correct: pairs twice, singletons three times and \(B\) four times. Complete-row summation then gives \(C_4<1/128\). All five three-parent seed shapes, both record-dependent cases, full complements and the empty-parent factor are accounted for.
- The hand comparisons correctly give \(M_5>5.12\) billion, \(T>465\) billion and \(U_6<369{,}664{,}456{,}005<T\). Five/six maxima and actual \(W\) remain open.
